title: Mixtape and Group Chat
premise: Cyrus Eriksen has perfected invisibility at Halloway High, but when her best friend Priya vanishes the night of the spring mixtape exchange, leaving only a keyring in Priya's locker, Cyrus is pulled into a group chat archive that reveals Priya was investigating who really stole the town's founding Mixtape tradition from its Black creators decades ago. Following keys, cassette fragments, and old yearbooks, Cyrus uncovers that the school board president's family erased the original founders' names, and that Priya's disappearance was no accident. In the end, Cyrus chooses visibility over safety, broadcasting the truth through prom itself, restoring the tradition to the founding families while Priya, found alive and hiding from retaliation, comes home.
about_author: Lior Voss is a former high-school debate coach who writes stories about quiet kids who find their volume. They live in a small river town where every diner jukebox still takes quarters.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. We meet her rules for invisibility at Halloway High: never raise your hand first, never sit center cafeteria. Her debate coach begs her to compete; she declines. Emotional beat: the ache of being excellent and unseen.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The annual spring mixtape exchange, a Halloway tradition older than the school itself. Priya hands Cyrus a tape labeled 'PLAY ME WHEN I'M GONE' as a joke. Laughter, cheap pizza, promises about prom. Beat: warmth before the fall.

chapters.title: Locker 114
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, next morning. Priya doesn't show. Police call it a runaway. In Priya's locker: a keyring with seven unlabeled keys and nothing else. Beat: dread arriving quietly, like weather.

chapters.title: Play Me When I'm Gone
chapters.summary: Cyrus listens to the tape alone: half music, half Priya whispering clues—'the chat remembers what they deleted.' Beat: fear sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Seven Keys
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. She maps the keys: gym storage, the library annex, the historical society, the band room, the bus depot, the old Elam house, and one she can't place. First key opens the gym loft. Beat: the hunt begins.

chapters.title: The Group Chat That Wouldn't Die
chapters.summary: Dual POV begins—alternating Cyrus and Priya's recovered messages. The archived chat shows Priya interviewing elders about the Mixtape's origins. Beat: grief braided with discovery.

chapters.title: The Founders Nobody Names
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. At the historical society, she finds the 1968 photo: the Mixtape dance was created by three Black families—the Elams, the Okonkwos, the Brights—whose names were later scrubbed from plaques. Beat: righteous anger.

chapters.title: Board President Whitlock
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. She cautiously questions Marcus Whitlock, whose grandfather 'founded' the tradition per official record. His charm has cracks. Beat: first contact with the antagonist.

chapters.title: Key Five: The Depot
chapters.summary: Priya's POV via journal entries hidden with the depot key. She'd found proof Whitlock's family paid the school to rewrite history—and someone had followed her home. Beat: rising menace.

chapters.title: Home Is an Argument
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Her parents, terrified, forbid the investigation; the debate champion loses every round at her own dinner table. Beat: isolation deepening.

chapters.title: Dex and the Band Room
chapters.summary: Cyrus recruits Dex, Priya's ex-bandmate, breaking her own invisibility rule. The band room key yields a recording of Whitlock's father threatening the Elams in 1989. Beat: alliance forged.

chapters.title: The Old Elam House
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Mrs. Elam, ninety-one, tells her the whole story and gives her the missing seventh key's purpose: the time capsule under the gym floor. Beat: inheritance of memory.

chapters.title: Someone Knows
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Her locker is ransacked; the tape is gone. A note: 'Runaways stay gone.' Beat: terror made personal.

chapters.title: What Priya Found
chapters.summary: Priya's POV, the night she vanished: she confronted Whitlock's son, was chased, and went dark deliberately to protect Cyrus. Beat: relief and heartbreak—she chose silence like Cyrus always did.

chapters.title: Prom Is Cancelled
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The board cancels prom citing 'vandalism,' burying the capsule site under renovation permits. Beat: the stakes crystallize—tradition versus erasure.

chapters.title: Debate Champion
chapters.summary: Cyrus finally competes—not in a tournament but at a packed school-board forum, dismantling the renovation vote on record. Beat: the invisible girl finds her voice.

chapters.title: Seventh Key
chapters.summary: Cyrus, Dex, and Mrs. Elam's grandson open the time capsule days before the concrete pour: founding tapes, signed agreements, the original names. Beat: triumph shadowed by urgency.

chapters.title: Whitlock's Counterpunch
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Whitlock accuses Cyrus of theft and vandalism; police visit her home. Her parents, seeing her courage, finally stand with her. Beat: lowest point before the climb.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax. During the emergency board session, Cyrus plays the 1989 recording and the founders' tapes over the gym PA as students flood in. Whitlock's son breaks and confesses what happened the night Priya ran. Beat: truth detonating in public.

chapters.title: Where Priya Was
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Following the confession, they find Priya safe at her aunt's two towns over, having waited out the threats. Reunion at the bus depot, the sixth key turning in Cyrus's palm. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: The Mixtape Restored
chapters.summary: Resolution begins. Prom happens—renamed the Founders' Mixtape Ball—with the Elam, Okonkwo, and Bright names read aloud. Cyrus DJs the first set. Beat: joy as justice.

chapters.title: Visible
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, final chapter. She accepts the debate captaincy, keeps Priya's tape unplayed forever, and adds her own name to the plaque committee. Beat: identity claimed, memory kept, silence ended.
